question: Does requiring the exact oriented cubic resolvent polynomial silently impose elliptic rational solubility on an otherwise valid unramified S4 class?
gate: Derive the norm-square quartic and its trace-free resolvent. Fixing the latter to the original cubic should be equivalent to rational solubility on the minus-one twist. Test this on the six generic strict classes whose nondegenerate twist CT restriction is already certified.
inputs: Only the reference cubic, its field discriminant, six generic strict representatives and the unconditional rank-six twist CT matrix. No exceptional point, class or rank label. Frozen existing generic control, not a sample chosen for a new correlation.
failure: UNKNOWN on a failed certificate or absent prime witness. No failure to represent a class with one oriented resolvent is interpreted as absence of the underlying class field. Field discriminant equality is deduced from retained strictness, not certified by a fresh maximal-order computation.
